title: The Blue Notebook Review: Arrests are up &  Officer Avila is "Missing"
description:
Get the facts on what your SMPD is doing citywide! In this week's Blue Notebook Review:

🛣️The HLP team & partners clear a massive 5,000lb encampment near the I-10.
🛑Traffic enforcement... The California Roll
🔎 Where's Neighborhood Resource Officer Avila? 

All this and more!
transcript_text: Good morning, Santa Monica. My name is Sergeant Rick with the San Police Department, and this is your Blue Notebook review. Before we get started, I want to share some stats with you that even our most critical viewers are going to have a hard time talking smack about. So, year to date, we respond to 16,415 calls for service. That alone isn't what I'm referencing because you guys already know how busy we are. Uh that is an 18% increase from last year at this time. But the number I'm talking about is we've made 636 arrests so far this year. But Sergeant Rick, why is that so significant? Ha. Last year that number was at 371, which means 71% increase in arrests. That is what I'm talking about. And I am so proud of our police department. Now, I am so proud of your police department because we're out there doing the work for you. So, let's hear from our neighborhood resource officers to tell you what those numbers actually entail. Officer Hollowell, looks like you're at one of my favorite parks, Virginia Avenue Park. Let's hear from you first. >> Thanks, Sarge. Officer Steven Hollowell, your B1 neighborhood resource officer here in the field. And for this operational period for crime suppression, Santa Monica Police Department officers responded to 2,856 calls for service as well as conducted 100 arrests. Good job. And as for the two incidents that I'm going to discuss today, Santa Monica Police Sea Watch patrol officers respond to an armed robbery that just occurred at Second and California. With the assistance of the Smart Center, we were able to track the fleeing suspects. SeaWatch officers engaged in a pursuit to our neighboring jurisdiction with the assistance of Los Angeles Police Department Air16. Upon the termination of pursuit, five suspects were taken into custody with the assistance of K92 officer Bakarella and K9 Frankie. So guess what? Bing bong for five suspects in custody. Good job. Way to put bad guys in jail. And as for the second incident, downtown service unit responded and were conducting crime suppression in the 1500 block of alley 4 when they observed a hand to hand. A hand to hand for those who don't know is that narcotics suspicious activity. Upon stopping and detaining those people, they were able to come in contact and found 21 grams of fentanyl and 7 g of methamphetamine. Great job. Great obskills. Way to work the beat. And this is Stephen Hollowwell in the field. Back to you in the studio. Sarge. See you later. >> Thanks, Stephen. Another week of 100 plus arrests. That's now week four or five in a row of over 100 arrests. And great job, Frankie. Frankie is one of our our New Yorker kines. And in a future, Rick, if you can get a good photo of Frankie in time for this episode to come out, can you put it right here for us? Thank you. And let's keep this momentum going and talk about homelessness with Officer Tago who looks to be at one of our local skate parks. Officer Tago, what do you got? Thanks, Arch. Hello, Santa Monica. Officer Tago here, your B3 neighborhood resource officer. During this reporting period, help stay active across the city. They focus on our parks, downtown area, beach areas, and freeway underpasses. Wherever the issues were servicing, that's where we focus our time. Consistent presence, no shortcuts. Officers made over 30 misdemeanor and felony arrests tied to public camping, parole violations, narcotic offenses, sex offender registration violations, and outstanding warrants. Many of these involve repeat behavior, so enforcement was necessary to address ongoing quality of life impacts in our public spaces. At the same time, we continued working closely with the Department of Mental Health, Santa Monica's host team, code enforcement, and outreach partners. When someone was open to services, we connected them. When the laws were being ignored, we took action. That balance is part of the job, but accountability is always clear. By the numbers, our help team responded to 255 radio calls, conducted 221 self initiated contacts, addressed nine encampments, made 31 arrest, and conducted five mental health evaluations. An instant of note, near the I 10 at Lincoln, officers continue addressing freeway and bankman encampments, working alongside host and merapostal landscaping. Over 5,000 lbs of trash was removed. That's more than two and a half tons clear from one of the busiest gateways into our city, reducing fire hazards, improving visibility, and restoring that corridor for everyone who travels through it. We're going to keep addressing issues directly and staying consistent across the city, steady, grounded, and focused. That work doesn't stop, and neither do we. And from the co here at Memorial Park, back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Oh, look, Toggle. I can point my camera upwards, too, to make me look bigger, but I won't. because I got nothing to prove. But in all seriousness, he did touch on a good point in in regard to the repeat violators that won't be tolerated. So, Chief Jacob has made it clear to the troops that we're not looking the other way. If someone comes into the city of Santa Monica and commits a crime, they will be held accountable. Hence why our numbers are so high now. So, let's turn it over to Officer Partardo to talk about traffic enforcement. Izzy, what do you got? Hello Santa Monica, welcome back. Traffic enforcement remained active citywide with focused attention on school zones, downtown Santa Monica, Pacific Coast Highway, and other high collision corridors. High visibility operations targeted speed, distracted driving, equipment violations, and DUI enforcement, deploying officers where collision trends, and community concerns showed the greatest need. Community service officers also played a critical role by documenting collisions, completing reports, and assisting with traffic control, keeping sworn officers available for high priority calls while ensuring accurate reporting. During this period, officers conducted 298 traffic stops and issued 155 citations. Notably, both stops and citations are down compared to prior weeks, reflecting the impact of sustained enforcement efforts. I call that a win. When we hit the streets proactively, behavior adjusts. Visibility actually really works. A few quick did you know reminders. The most common primary collision factors remain unsafe speed, distracted driving, and failure to yield right away. Secondly, using your phone at a red light is still a vehicle code of violation. If you're not legally parked, it doesn't count. At that California roll through a stop sign, still a violation. Bull stops prevent real crashes. Most collisions aren't complicated, they're preventable. Drive focused, drive smart. And that's all I have. Back to you in the studio, Sarge. >> Great point, Izzy. Look, contrary to popular belief, we don't want to have to write tickets. If we go a shift and everyone's just obeying traffic laws and and traffic's flowing smoothly and there's no traffic collisions and no one's getting hurt, like, that would be ideal. But unfortunately, some of y'all need a little red and blue light reminder of what you can and cannot do. But I digress. Last but not least, let's head over to Officer Aila to talk about our community engagement. Brandon, it's good to see that you're still part of our unit. What do you got? >> Thank you, sir. Hello, Blue Notebook family. Today, we're out here at Lincoln Middle School for our Cops and Cleat event. We brought the mounting unit with us today. I would like to start off by saying thank you to my internal affairs sergeants for that amazing interview last week. Turn the page. No, I am not being forced to say this, nor was I given a script to read. My internal affairs sergeants are very hardworking and amazing. Give two thumbs up. >> Here with me today is our crime prevention coordinators for beats three and >> uh looks like we lost them. Alexis, can you get him back on? No. Well, that's show biz for you. Not bad. I think four weeks of doing the blue notebook with Anna Rose and this is our first hiccup. Well, future Rick, if you can figure out something to put in place of all that, now's your chance. And that, my friends, concludes this week's Blue Notebook review. Time for the top comment of the week. And that goes to me. Just want to take a moment. Uh, if you saw one of our most recent social media posts, Matt and Lana from Shoes on Main Street, they are retiring. After being here for over 20 years, they finally decided to go enjoy retirement. So, Matt and Lana, thank you. We appreciate you. Thank you for the great food and and for the countless laughs and and through everything through the darkest times, through the best of times, like you guys have always been a staple in this city. So, thank you guys. Enjoy retirement.
